title: RBAC v2 migration: wave orchestration and audit-trail failsafes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Execute a safe, observable, and reversible migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 across hosted and Dedicated customers. This ticket covers orchestration of migration waves by customer tier, dual-write strategy and reconciliation, audit-log preservation and augmentation, SSO/SAML attribute validation, and new admin controls to prevent privilege loss during cutover. Success criteria: (1) automated parity verification passes for >99% of traffic in canary wave, (2) no loss of audit records and full continuity of native audit IDs, (3) rapid rollback path validated end-to-end, (4) customer comms templates and KB published for opt-in/opt-out flows.
comments: 2025-02-06 - Kickoff: scoped three migration waves (internal-only, low-risk customers, high-risk customers). Decided to introduce a short opt-in window for non-critical customers before forced migration. Action: create opt-in UI and CLI flags.

2025-02-12 - Design review with Security and Product: agreed to preserve v1 audit ids as metadata on v2 events and forward both to centralized audit pipeline. Security requested immutable event checksum to detect tampering.

2025-02-20 - Engineering spike: built reconciliation prototype that dual-writes to v1 authority store and new v2 role-store with idempotent semantics. Found edge-case where cached role bindings for long-running sessions aren't invalidated; added KV cache eviction hook to runtime (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/PR-248).
2025-02-28 - Observability planning: dashboards wired for 'role parity drift' metric, reconciliation success rate, and audit-lag histogram. Pager runbook drafted for parity drop below 99.5%.

2025-03-04 - SSO mapping: added attribute validation harness that replays SAML assertions against mapping rules and emits mapping-diff artifacts. Test run against 12 enterprise SSO configs found 3 mapping exceptions; reached out to SEs for remediation.

2025-03-08 - Canary prep: automated acceptance tests created (conformance-suite) to validate authorization decisions against golden fixtures. Tests run in nightly CI and gated behind feature-flag 'rbac_v2_dualwrite'.
2025-03-11 - Communications: drafted customer email and KB article template for opt-in, migration timeline, and rollback guarantee. Included CLI rollback command examples and support contact paths.

2025-03-12 - Current blockers: waiting on dedicated infra quota for canary wave and final sign-off on security review checklist. Action owners: Infra (Natasha) to allocate capacity; Security (Omar) to finish review by 2025-03-15.
runbook_summary: Staged waves: 1) Internal + infra smoke, 2) Low-risk customers (no SSO custom mappings), 3) High-risk enterprise customers with negotiated maintenance windows. For each wave: enable dual-write -> run parity checks for 48h -> enable audit-id preservation middleware -> flip read-path to v2 for a small percentage of traffic -> ramp to 100% reads -> monitor parity & error budgets for 72h -> schedule final cutover. Rollback: feature-flag disable dual-write + point reads back to v1 authority store; run reconciliation to reconcile writes since rollback window; notify customers and open postmortem if parity < 99%.
verification_steps: Automated conformance-suite passes (authz decisions, negative tests, edge bindings)
Parity metric >= 99.5% for 72 hours during canary
Audit trail continuity validated: v1_id present as metadata and event checksum matches historical stream
SSO mapping diff reports show zero unresolved exceptions (or documented customer action)
Reconciliation job completes within SLA and reports zero dangerous deltas
post_migration_tasks: Migrate long-term audit storage index to include v2 IDs and composite keys
Deprecate v1 admin APIs behind a 1-month eol after all customers migrated
Publish 'what changed' KB for admin console UI and role templates
Run internal training with Support and SE teams including simulated incident playbook
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Role-binding drift for long-lived KV cache entries. Mitigation: add eviction hook and conservative TTL, monitor cache-miss surge
Risk: SSO attribute mismatch causing access regression for small subset. Mitigation: opt-in window + mapping-harness + SE-assisted remediation
Risk: Audit gap during switchover. Mitigation: dual-write with event checksum and native audit-id passthrough; export to external SIEM while validating continuity
Risk: Customer trust impact. Mitigation: clear comms, rollback guarantee, and dedicated support channel during waves
customer_communications: Low-risk customers: 2-week notice email with opt-in link and CLI examples; support hours limited to business hours
Enterprise customers: schedule a working session, provide migration checklist, allow maintenance window or opt-out for 30 days
Post-cutover: summary email with audit logs pointer and link to KB on how to verify their roles
